To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acute lithium treatment before ischemia, reduces voltage decay and the time of the fast decay rate, and increases time constant decay during global ischemia.

acute lithium infusion, 20 min before global ischemia, reduces the decay rate and duration of fast decay phase, as well as increasing the time constant of impedance decay during global ischemia, in an animal model of global ischemia.

acute lithium infusion (10 mg·kg(- 1) Li₂CO₃ i.v.) 20 min before global ischemia, reduces brain impedance by reducing the voltage decay rate and the time constant of the fast phase, and by increasing the time constant of slow phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential effects of lithium treatment in the acute phase of global cerebral ischemia.
the time course of the acute effects of lithium on global cerebral ischemia, as measured by brain impedance.
the acute effects of lithium on the brain, in the early phases of cerebral ischemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
acute lithium treatment, at any dose, induces a strong reduction of cerebral edema, as measured by brain impedance.
acute lithium infusion, at any dose, induces a strong reduction in brain edema, and that this reduction is more effective at 100 mg·lithium·kg(-1).
lithium, at the doses tested, induces a neuroprotective acute effect that could be useful in clinical situations where a fast response is needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
acute lithium treatment reduces the brain edema induced by global cerebral ischemia.
acute lithium administration, at low doses, reduces brain edema and the duration of fast decay of brain impedance in the early phase of global ischemia.
acute treatment of lithium before and during the first minutes of ischemia may have a neuroprotective effect, which is more intense than that of chronic treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

acute lithium administration is neuroprotective, and that this protection is effective at low doses, and is more intense in the fast phase of brain edema, and that the neuroprotection is effective in both the acute and chronic phases of ischemia.
lithium has a fast and strong effect in reducing brain impedance, which is a measure of brain edema.
lithium has acute neuroprotective actions in global cerebral ischemia, which may be related to its ability to reduce brain edema.
